Assume countable choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and let $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Every smoothly embedded two-sphere in the interior of $E_K$ bounds a smoothly embedded closed three-ball contained in $E_K$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot that is not ambient isotopic to the standard unknot, let $E_K$ be its chosen compact exterior, and let $T_K=\partial E_K$. There is no properly embedded disk $D\subset E_K$ whose boundary is a simple closed curve in $T_K$ that is not null-homotopic in $T_K$.

For every smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1	o S^3$, let $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$ be the quotient normal bundle. Orient its two-dimensional fibres so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a positive basis of the normal fibre gives the fixed orientation of $S^3$. Then $
u_K$ admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism $
u_K\cong K	imes\mathbb R^2$.

Let $P$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a boundaryless Hausdorff smooth manifold, and let $i:P\to N$ be a smooth embedding. Let $Z\subset N$ be a closed embedded smooth submanifold without boundary. If $i$ is transverse to $Z$ along $\partial P$, then an arbitrarily small jointly smooth ambient isotopy, supported in any prescribed neighborhood of $i(P)$ and fixed on a neighborhood of $i(\partial P)$, makes $i(P)$ transverse to $Z$. The isotopy may be stationary near its time endpoints. No choice axiom is assumed. The same assertion holds for any finite family of such $Z$, provided the initial boundary restriction is transverse to every member. Empty source and empty intersection are allowed.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth knot and let $A(M,L)$ be either its ordinary or its enhanced A-polynomial. The exponent point $(a,b)$ denotes $L^aM^b$. For every one-dimensional edge of its Newton polygon there are an irreducible factor $P$ of $A$, its peripheral curve $Y\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$, a local DVR $R$ of a normalized complex curve with fraction field $\mathbb C(Y)$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbb C(Y)$ with an extending normalized discrete valuation $w$, with the following properties.

There is an actual representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(E)$ and a common peripheral eigenline whose eigenvalues are the coordinate functions $M,L$ of $Y$. If $(u,v)$ is a primitive integral normal to the specified edge, oriented so that this edge minimizes its scalar product with the exponent polygon, then
$$\bigl(w(L),w(M)\bigr)=d(u,v)\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}).$$
The valuation is at a boundary branch of $Y$, since at least one coordinate has nonzero valuation; it is not an affine branch of $Y$. For the enhanced polynomial, the representation may be chosen absolutely irreducible. This additional clause uses the actual irreducible-character origin of its factors, and is not asserted for the ordinary abelian factor. No tree or essential surface is supplied by this lemma.

Assume full AC. Let $N$ be a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold whose boundary is a torus with supplied smooth meridian-longitude coordinates. Suppose $N$ is irreducible and its boundary is incompressible. Let $F/\mathbb C$ be a finitely generated field of transcendence degree one, equipped with the discrete valuation $v:F^*\to\mathbb Z$ at a point of a supplied smooth curve model, and let $\rho:\Gamma=\pi_1(N)\to SL_2(F)$ be a representation. Suppose its two commuting peripheral matrices have a common eigenline over $F$, with eigenvalues $L,M\in F^*$, and
$$\bigl(v(L),v(M)\bigr)\ne(0,0).$$
Then $N$ contains a compact connected neatly properly embedded orientable smooth surface $S$ with nonempty boundary, no compressing disk, no boundary-compressing disk, and no boundary-parallel component. Every boundary circle represents the unique primitive unoriented class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ satisfying
$$a\,v(L)+b\,v(M)=0.$$
The surface is obtained from an actual equivariant map of the universal cover into the lattice tree by finite component deletions and compression homotopies. Each lifted surface component maps to one edge midpoint, and each complementary lifted component maps into the corresponding midpoint-complement component.

If $\rho$ is absolutely irreducible, $S$ is not a fiber of any fibration $N\to S^1$ with fiber $S$. No ideal point, Newton edge, or existence of this representation is inferred by this theorem; those are separate algebraic inputs.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A simple closed curve on a surface is **essential** if it is not null-homotopic there. A surface $S\subset E_K$ is properly embedded if $S\cap\partial E_K=\partial S$ and its interior lies in the interior of $E_K$. It is **incompressible** if it has no embedded disk with interior disjoint from $S$ and essential boundary in $S$; it is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no embedded disk whose boundary is the union of an arc in $S$ that does not cut off a disk and an arc in $\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as the boundary of a properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.

derivations.claim: Let $e$ be any edge of the ordinary Newton polygon. Apply [F2] to the ordinary polynomial: it selects an irreducible peripheral curve factor with parallel minimum face, constructs the boundary-branch DVR by the unimodular toric chart, selects an actual finite-field generic representation by a closed point of the nonzero incidence fiber, and extends the valuation to that field. If $(u,v)$ is the primitive minimum normal in exponent coordinates $(a,b)$, its eigenvalues satisfy $(w(L),w(M))=d(u,v)$ for an integer $d>0$. Nothing in this step assumes that this ordinary representation is irreducible; it includes the abelian $L-1$ factor.

The manifold hypotheses of [F3] are exactly [F1]. Its valued-field hypotheses are supplied by step 1.1, and the valuation pair is nonzero. Thus [F3] gives a connected orientable neatly properly embedded smooth surface with nonempty boundary, no compression or boundary compression, and primitive boundary class $(a,b)$ satisfying $au+bv=0$. This is an actual associated midpoint surface after the finite compression and deletion homotopies, not an assumed Culler–Shalen witness.

Every direction $(\Delta a,\Delta b)$ of the original edge also satisfies $u\Delta a+v\Delta b=0$. Consequently its extended rational slope $\Delta b/\Delta a$ is exactly $b/a$ by [F4], including the vertical case where both denominators vanish and the value is infinity. This is a boundary slope realized by the surface of step 2.1, as required. The proof uses only the ordinary branch of [F2]–[F3] and makes no nonfiber or strictness assertion for that branch.

citations.quote: Assume full AC. Let $X$ be an irreducible component of the $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety of a knot exterior that contains irreducible characters and has a nonempty dense Zariski-open locus of scheme-smooth admissible characters whose peripheral restriction is not boundary-parabolic. Here boundary-parabolic means that every peripheral word has trace $2$ or $-2$; since the meridian and longitude commute and generate the peripheral group, this is equivalent to both $(\operatorname{tr}\rho(\mu))^2=4$ and $(\operatorname{tr}\rho(\lambda))^2=4$. Thus “not boundary-parabolic” means that at least one of those two trace squares differs from $4$. On this locus the Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is invariant under conjugation and extends to a rational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)$; when $X$ is one-dimensional its generic value lies in $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C(X))$, and unless it is identically $\infty$ it is an ordinary rational function in $\mathbb C(X)$.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ have admissible adjoint local system, and let $v_\rho$ be a nonzero peripheral-adjoint-invariant vector for which $[v_\rho\otimes\lambda],[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$ form the specified ordered basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}\rho)$. If a generator of the one-dimensional kernel of inclusion is $a[v_\rho\otimes\lambda]+b[v_\rho\otimes\mu]$, the **Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope** is $s_K(\rho)=-b/a\in\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. Rescaling $v_\rho$ or the kernel generator does not change this projective ratio. A rational function on an irreducible character component means an element of its function field, the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A projective-valued rational function means a point of the projective line over that field; it may be identically $\infty$. The slope's rational extension has this projective meaning. Unless its generic value is $\infty$, it is an ordinary rational function, whose individual infinite values are poles. Its rational extension is not a value assigned to every singular or inadmissible character.

Assume full AC. Let $E$ be the compact exterior of a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, with positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Let $X$ be an irreducible one-dimensional component of its complex $SL_2$ character variety. Fix a one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue-image component $Y$ arising from $X$, with coordinates $(M,L)$ ordered as (meridian,longitude), and an irreducible Laurent equation $P(M,L)=0$ for $Y$. Write $K=\mathbb C(X)$.

There is a finite extension $F/K$ with an actual generic representation $\rho:\pi_1(E)\to SL_2(F)$ and a choice of common peripheral eigenline whose eigenvalues are $M,L\in F^*$. These give the specified generic point of $Y$. Its actual intrinsic adjoint peripheral homology has a two-dimensional boundary basis ordered (longitude,meridian) and a one-dimensional inclusion kernel. With $\delta\in\{\lambda,\mu\}$ having distinct peripheral eigenvalues, set $u=\rho(\delta)-\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\delta))I/2$. In that basis its kernel is exactly
$$\ker\left\{F^2\longrightarrow\Omega^1_{F/\mathbb C},\quad (a,b)\longmapsto a\,\frac{\mathrm dL}{L}+b\,\frac{\mathrm dM}{M}\right\}.$$
The two displayed differentials are not both zero. Thus its projective slope, with convention $s=-b/a$ for the kernel line, is
$$s=\left[\frac{\mathrm dL}{L}:\frac{\mathrm dM}{M}\right]=[-M P_M:L P_L]\ \in\mathbb P^1(F).$$
A ratio of one-forms here means their coordinate pair in any nonzero basis of the one-dimensional $F$-space $\Omega^1_{F/\mathbb C}$. The result is independent of that basis, the finite field model, the common eigenline and simultaneous conjugation, and is defined over $K$. It includes zero when $\mathrm dL=0$ and infinity when $\mathrm dM=0$. In particular a nonconstant meridian eigenvalue is not assumed.

This is an identity of rational projective maps. It agrees with the actual specialized homology slope on a nonempty dense rank-chart open. At every point where the rational extension and the peripheral restriction are evaluated and $(P_M,P_L)\ne(0,0)$, its projective value is $[-M P_M:L P_L]$; when $P_L\ne0$ this is the ordinary value $-M P_M/(L P_L)$. For the square-free ordinary A-polynomial, replacing $P$ by the full polynomial gives the same ratio at a point where its gradient is nonzero. No assertion that all specialized exterior homology ranks are constant outside that open, nor any ideal-point tree or essential-surface construction, is part of this lemma.

Assume full AC. Let $F/\mathbb C$ be a finitely generated field of transcendence degree one, and let $R=A_{\mathfrak m}\subset F$ be the local ring at a complex point of a curve, where $A$ is a finitely generated complex domain with fraction field $F$. Suppose $R$ is the actual DVR local ring of the given smooth point, with residue field $\mathbb C$, valuation $v$ and uniformizer $t$.

The derivation $D$ with $Dt=1$ extends uniquely from $\mathbb C(t)$ to $F$, satisfies $D(R)\subseteq R$, and for every $f\in F^*$ has
$$t\,\frac{Df}{f}\in R,\qquad \overline{t\,Df/f}=v(f)\in\mathbb C.$$
For $L,M\in F^*$ with $(v(L),v(M))\ne(0,0)$, the rational projective logarithmic ratio extends at the point with value
$$\left[\frac{\mathrm dL}{L}:\frac{\mathrm dM}{M}\right]_{x}=[v(L):v(M)].$$
The ratio of one-forms means their two coefficients in any common nonzero basis of $\Omega^1_{F/\mathbb C}$.

In particular the nonzero-valuation condition always holds when $F=\mathbb C(Y)$ for an irreducible affine curve $Y\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$ with coordinate functions $M,L$, its normalization $U$ is the given dense affine open of a separated smooth completion $C$, and $x\in C\setminus U$ is an ideal point with the above local data. Singular affine branches retained in $U$ are not mistaken for ideal points.

For every finite field extension $F'/F$, an extending discrete valuation $w$ exists with residue field $\mathbb C$ and restriction $w|_{F^*}=e v$ for an integer $e>0$. More generally, suppose any field extension $F'/F$ is supplied with a discrete valuation $w$ restricting to $e v$ on $F^*$ for a positive integer $e$. Let a representation into $SL_2(F')$ have commuting peripheral matrices $\rho(\lambda),\rho(\mu)$ with a common eigenline of eigenvalues $L,M$. Use the valuation-ring lattice graph of [[def-adjoint-twisted-homology-and-culler-shalen-data]]. If the element $\rho(\lambda^a\mu^b)$ fixes a vertex or the midpoint of an edge, then
$$a\,v(L)+b\,v(M)=0.$$
For a primitive nonzero pair $(a,b)$ and a nonzero valuation pair it follows that the logarithmic projective limit is $[-b:a]$, the negative of the boundary slope $r=b/a$, including zero and infinity.

This applies in particular to a supplied equivariant map from the universal cover of a knot exterior to that lattice graph whenever a component of a transverse inverse image of the edge midpoints has a boundary circle representing $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$. It does not assert that the graph is a tree, that such a map or an essential surface exists, that a character ideal point must be a peripheral ideal point, or that every possible boundary-elliptic surface choice has a prescribed slope. Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, $E_K$ its exterior, and $ho:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C)$ a representation. The **adjoint local system** $\operatorname{Ad}ho$ has fibre $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ and left group-module action $\gamma\cdot v=ho(\gamma)vho(\gamma)^{-1}$. In the first-loop-first intrinsic convention, this means forward path transport $T_\gamma(v)=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$; equivalently the corresponding right action is $v\cdot\gamma=ho(\gamma)^{-1}vho(\gamma)$. Its twisted homology $H_*(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ is the intrinsic local-system homology with these transports, equivalently the homology of the cellular local-coefficient complex for a supplied CW structure; the same convention defines boundary-torus twisted homology and the inclusion map $i_*:H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)	o H_1(E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$. An **admissible adjoint representation** is one for which there is a nonzero vector $v_ho\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ fixed by the peripheral adjoint action such that $\{[v_ho\otimes\lambda],[v_ho\otimes\mu]\}$ is a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\operatorname{Ad}ho)$ and $\ker i_*$ is one-dimensional. For an irreducible affine character curve $X$, its function field $\mathbb C(X)$ is the fraction field of its coordinate domain. A **tautological representation** over $\mathbb C(X)$ is a homomorphism $ho_X:\pi_1(E_K)	o SL_2(\mathbb C(X))$ whose character is the generic character of $X$. A **smooth projective completion** consists of a smooth complete curve $\overline X$ with a dense open subset $U$ identified with the normalization $X^
u$ of $X$, with its finite birational normalization map $
u:U	o X$ recorded. When $X$ is smooth, $
u$ identifies $U$ with $X$, recovering the usual completion. An **ideal point** is a point $x\in\overline X\setminus U$; points of $U$ over singular affine points of $X$ are affine branches and are retained inside $U$. Such an ideal point defines the discrete valuation $v_x(f)=\operatorname{ord}_x(f)$ on $\mathbb C(X)$. The valuation ring is $\mathcal O_x=\{f:v_x(f)\ge0\}$, and a **uniformizer** is an element $\pi\in\mathcal O_x$ with $v_x(\pi)=1$. Its residue field is $k_x=\mathcal O_x/(\pi)$. An $\mathcal O_x$-lattice in $\mathbb C(X)^2$ is a free rank-two $\mathcal O_x$-submodule spanning $\mathbb C(X)^2$; two lattices are homothetic if one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other. The **Bruhat–Tits tree** has homothety classes of these lattices as vertices, with two vertices adjacent if representatives satisfy $\pi\Lambda\subsetneq\Lambda'\subsetneq\Lambda$ and $\Lambda/\Lambda'$ is one-dimensional over $k_x$. Whenever the tautological representation exists, it acts on this tree. The ideal point, valuation, action, and any essential surface produced from the action are its Culler–Shalen data; that surface is called the associated Culler–Shalen surface.

derivations.claim: **The rational affine identity.** By [F3], the actual generic peripheral inclusion kernel, in the ordered basis [F2], is the kernel of $(a,b)\mapsto a\,\mathrm dL/L+b\,\mathrm dM/M$. Its dimension is one, and the differential pair is nonzero. Differentiating $A_X(M,L)=0$ gives $$L(A_X)_L\,\mathrm dL/L+M(A_X)_M\,\mathrm dM/M=0.$$ Therefore [F2] and [F3] give the projective rational slope $[-M(A_X)_M:L(A_X)_L]$. Its affine ratio at the stated smooth point is $-M(A_X)_M/(L(A_X)_L)$, since the denominator there is nonzero. The rational extension is the one constructed by [F3]; where [F1]'s hypotheses hold, it agrees with the extension recorded there. This identity therefore includes its values wherever that displayed denominator is nonzero and does not rely on an unproved identification of exceptional pointwise homology kernels.

**The peripheral ideal point and its actual valuation.** The curve whose completion occurs in the second clause is the preceding peripheral curve $A_X(M,L)=0$. Use its normalized affine open and the actual local DVR at its stipulated ideal point $x$, with valuation $v$. By [F4], $(v(L),v(M))\ne(0,0)$: if both coordinates were units, their affine coordinate ring and its integral closure would lie in the local DVR, and separatedness would put its center in that normalized affine open, contrary to idealness. The actual generic representation and common peripheral eigenline may be taken over a finite extension of this peripheral function field by [F3]: its field is finitely generated of transcendence degree one and finite over the field generated by the nonconstant coordinates $M,L$. By [F4] the valuation extends to this finite field, or to any further finite field used by the stipulated construction, with restriction $e v$ for an integer $e>0$. Thus no valuation on the representation field is merely assumed to exist.

**The boundary relation survives the stipulated construction.** Consider a surviving boundary circle of the associated essential surface, representing the primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ of its asserted boundary slope. Before the boundary-preserving compressions in [F5], that same circle is a boundary circle of the transverse inverse image of edge midpoints. A lift of the circle is connected and maps into the discrete midpoint set, so its image is one midpoint. Equivariance implies that its deck element fixes that midpoint. Access-path changes conjugate the element and the fixed point together. By [F4], its determinant-one peripheral matrix therefore has eigenvalue $L^aM^b$ of valuation zero: a fixed midpoint implies that its square fixes a lattice vertex, and the integral characteristic polynomial at that lattice excludes both positive and negative eigenvalue valuation. Consequently $$a\,v(L)+b\,v(M)=0.$$ An interior compression replaces an annular neighborhood of a circle in the interior of the surface by two disks in the interior of the exterior, and hence does not change the boundary one-manifold. Deleting a component only deletes its boundary circles. Boundary isotopy changes no homology class; orientation reversal changes both $a,b$ by a common sign. The same relation therefore holds for every boundary circle retained in the associated essential surface after these operations. This proves the boundary calculation for the actual stipulated construction; no essential-surface existence theorem or assertion about an unrelated vertex-stabilized surface is used.

**Evaluate the projective limit, including infinity.** By [F4], the rational logarithmic pair $[\mathrm dL/L:\mathrm dM/M]$ has value $[v(L):v(M)]$ at $x$. More explicitly, with a uniformizer $t$ and $D=\mathrm d/\mathrm dt$, writing $f=t^{v(f)}u$ gives $t Df/f=v(f)+t Du/u$, where $D$ preserves the actual local ring; the unit term vanishes on reduction. The valuation pair is nonzero by step 1.2. Its relation in step 2.1 identifies its projective line as $[-b:a]$. By step 1.1 this logarithmic pair is the rational slope, so its limiting value is $-b/a=-r$ in the fixed convention. The same homogeneous computation gives $0$ when $b=0$ and $\infty$ when $a=0$; neither case requires division by a zero valuation. All assertions of the Statement follow.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume countable choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and let $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Every smoothly embedded two-sphere in the interior of $E_K$ bounds a smoothly embedded closed three-ball contained in $E_K$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot that is not ambient isotopic to the standard unknot, let $E_K$ be its chosen compact exterior, and let $T_K=\partial E_K$. There is no properly embedded disk $D\subset E_K$ whose boundary is a simple closed curve in $T_K$ that is not null-homotopic in $T_K$.

For every smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1	o S^3$, let $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$ be the quotient normal bundle. Orient its two-dimensional fibres so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a positive basis of the normal fibre gives the fixed orientation of $S^3$. Then $
u_K$ admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism $
u_K\cong K	imes\mathbb R^2$.

Let $P$ be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a boundaryless Hausdorff smooth manifold, and let $i:P\to N$ be a smooth embedding. Let $Z\subset N$ be a closed embedded smooth submanifold without boundary. If $i$ is transverse to $Z$ along $\partial P$, then an arbitrarily small jointly smooth ambient isotopy, supported in any prescribed neighborhood of $i(P)$ and fixed on a neighborhood of $i(\partial P)$, makes $i(P)$ transverse to $Z$. The isotopy may be stationary near its time endpoints. No choice axiom is assumed. The same assertion holds for any finite family of such $Z$, provided the initial boundary restriction is transverse to every member. Empty source and empty intersection are allowed.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth knot and let $A(M,L)$ be either its ordinary or its enhanced A-polynomial. The exponent point $(a,b)$ denotes $L^aM^b$. For every one-dimensional edge of its Newton polygon there are an irreducible factor $P$ of $A$, its peripheral curve $Y\subset(\mathbb C^*)^2$, a local DVR $R$ of a normalized complex curve with fraction field $\mathbb C(Y)$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbb C(Y)$ with an extending normalized discrete valuation $w$, with the following properties.

There is an actual representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(E)$ and a common peripheral eigenline whose eigenvalues are the coordinate functions $M,L$ of $Y$. If $(u,v)$ is a primitive integral normal to the specified edge, oriented so that this edge minimizes its scalar product with the exponent polygon, then
$$\bigl(w(L),w(M)\bigr)=d(u,v)\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}).$$
The valuation is at a boundary branch of $Y$, since at least one coordinate has nonzero valuation; it is not an affine branch of $Y$. For the enhanced polynomial, the representation may be chosen absolutely irreducible. This additional clause uses the actual irreducible-character origin of its factors, and is not asserted for the ordinary abelian factor. No tree or essential surface is supplied by this lemma.

Assume full AC. Let $N$ be a compact connected orientable smooth three-manifold whose boundary is a torus with supplied smooth meridian-longitude coordinates. Suppose $N$ is irreducible and its boundary is incompressible. Let $F/\mathbb C$ be a finitely generated field of transcendence degree one, equipped with the discrete valuation $v:F^*\to\mathbb Z$ at a point of a supplied smooth curve model, and let $\rho:\Gamma=\pi_1(N)\to SL_2(F)$ be a representation. Suppose its two commuting peripheral matrices have a common eigenline over $F$, with eigenvalues $L,M\in F^*$, and
$$\bigl(v(L),v(M)\bigr)\ne(0,0).$$
Then $N$ contains a compact connected neatly properly embedded orientable smooth surface $S$ with nonempty boundary, no compressing disk, no boundary-compressing disk, and no boundary-parallel component. Every boundary circle represents the unique primitive unoriented class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ satisfying
$$a\,v(L)+b\,v(M)=0.$$
The surface is obtained from an actual equivariant map of the universal cover into the lattice tree by finite component deletions and compression homotopies. Each lifted surface component maps to one edge midpoint, and each complementary lifted component maps into the corresponding midpoint-complement component.

If $\rho$ is absolutely irreducible, $S$ is not a fiber of any fibration $N\to S^1$ with fiber $S$. No ideal point, Newton edge, or existence of this representation is inferred by this theorem; those are separate algebraic inputs.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with chosen compact exterior $E_K$ and boundary torus $T_K=\partial E_K$. A simple closed curve on a surface is **essential** if it is not null-homotopic there. A surface $S\subset E_K$ is properly embedded if $S\cap\partial E_K=\partial S$ and its interior lies in the interior of $E_K$. It is **incompressible** if it has no embedded disk with interior disjoint from $S$ and essential boundary in $S$; it is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no embedded disk whose boundary is the union of an arc in $S$ that does not cut off a disk and an arc in $\partial E_K$. A **boundary slope** of $K$ is the unoriented isotopy class of an essential simple closed curve on $T_K$ that occurs as the boundary of a properly embedded, orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface. Using the positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$ as a homology basis, a primitive class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has slope $b/a\in\mathbb Q\cup\{\infty\}$, with $a=0$ interpreted as $\infty$. A boundary slope is **strict** if it has a realizing orientable, incompressible, boundary-incompressible surface which is not a fiber of any locally trivial fibration $E_K\to S^1$; a fiber is the inverse image of a point under that bundle projection.

derivations.claim: Let $e$ be any edge of the enhanced Newton polygon. By [F2], choose its minimum-normal valued model using the irreducible-character incidence charts in that supplier, not merely a factor of the ordinary polynomial. The finite word-matrix determinant certificate is inverted before the generic-fiber closed point is selected; hence it stays nonzero in the resulting finite field. Thus the constructed representation is absolutely irreducible, its peripheral eigenvalues are the actual coordinate functions, and their valuation pair is a positive multiple of the primitive normal to $e$. This also treats a factor $L-1$ contributed by irreducible characters.

Apply [F3] in the exterior verified by [F1]. It yields a connected orientable essential surface with nonempty boundary and the primitive kernel slope of that nonzero valuation pair. That is the edge slope by the same orthogonality equation as in [F4]. Moreover the last clause of [F3] applies to the ACTUAL absolutely irreducible representation from step 1.1. If the selected component were a fiber, its normal subgroup would fix an edge; integrality of all stable-letter conjugates would force the representation to be reducible, the contradiction proved there. Thus this surface is not a fiber of any fibration having it as fiber.

The surface is precisely a realizing orientable incompressible boundary-incompressible nonfiber surface in [F4]'s definition of strict boundary slope. Hence every specified enhanced edge slope is strict, including zero or infinity when those occur. No claim that the ordinary abelian $L-1$ edge is strict has been used: enhanced strictness depends on the actual irreducible-character model, while the ordinary boundary-slope theorem retains its weaker valid conclusion.

A projective-valued rational function means a point of the projective line over that field; it may be identically $\infty$. The slope's rational extension has this projective meaning. Assume full AC. Let $E$ be the compact exterior of a smooth oriented knot in $S^3$, with positive meridian $\mu$ and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Its actual intrinsic adjoint peripheral homology has a two-dimensional boundary basis ordered (longitude,meridian) and a one-dimensional inclusion kernel. With $\delta\in\{\lambda,\mu\}$ having distinct peripheral eigenvalues, set $u=\rho(\delta)-\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\delta))I/2$. In that basis its kernel is exactly
$$\ker\left\{F^2\longrightarrow\Omega^1_{F/\mathbb C},\quad (a,b)\longmapsto a\,\frac{\mathrm dL}{L}+b\,\frac{\mathrm dM}{M}\right\}.$$

$$s=\left[\frac{\mathrm dL}{L}:\frac{\mathrm dM}{M}\right]=[-M P_M:L P_L]\ \in\mathbb P^1(F).$$

This is an identity of rational projective maps. It agrees with the actual specialized homology slope on a nonempty dense rank-chart open. derivations.claim: **The exact full slope set.** Write $\mathcal S(K)=\{p/q\in\mathbb Q:\gcd(p,q)=1,\ q>0,\ E_K(p/q)\text{ is SU2-abelian}\}$. Its elements are DISTINCT slopes, not a selected sequence. The meridional slope $\infty$ is isolated and is not a finite-surgery parameter in this set. A simultaneous peripheral diagonalization of an SU2 representation gives $\rho(\mu)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\alpha},e^{-i\alpha})$ and $\rho(\lambda)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\beta},e^{-i\beta})$. The simultaneous inversion $(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(-\alpha,-\beta)$ is the pillowcase quotient. For any continuous lifted path through peripheral images of irreducible representations, a slope in $\mathcal S(K)$ satisfies $p\alpha(t)+q\beta(t)\notin2\pi\mathbb Z$: equality would give an actual irreducible representation of the filled group, contradicting [F1]. Continuity puts this entire real function in one component of $\mathbb R\setminus2\pi\mathbb Z$. Thus for ANY two points of that path, $|p(\alpha_1-\alpha_0)+q(\beta_1-\beta_0)|<2\pi.$ This is a full-set exclusion, valid for positive, negative and zero numerators.

**The exact instanton interface selects a nonvertical path.** Under [L1], its first alternative makes $\mathcal S(K)$ empty: for any finite $p/q$ choose $\beta=-p\pi/(2q)$ modulo $2\pi$ on that full vertical circle, giving an actual irreducible filling representation. Hence an SU2-averse knot, for which $\mathcal S(K)$ is infinite, must satisfy the second alternative. On a smaller closed subinterval its meridian is noncentral and already diagonal. Its commuting longitude is diagonal too; its eigenvalue is a continuous circle-valued function, so subdivision into finitely many open semicircle charts gives a continuous real lift $\beta$. The meridian coordinate $\alpha=s$ has distinct endpoint values. This is the ONLY use of [L1] in the subsequent path argument; no bare nontrivial-knot representation-existence assertion is silently substituted for its varying-meridian conclusion.

**Boundedness of ALL slopes.** Fix such a nonvertical path and endpoints, put $d=\alpha_1-\alpha_0\ne0$, $r_0=-(\beta_1-\beta_0)/d$ and $C=2\pi/|d|$. Step1.1 gives $|p/q-r_0|<C/q\le C$ for EVERY $p/q\in\mathcal S(K)$. Thus the full set is contained in the fixed bounded interval $[r_0-C,r_0+C]$; an unbounded exceptional subsequence is excluded. In a bounded interval there are only finitely many reduced fractions with denominator at most any fixed $Q$: for each $1\le q\le Q$ only finitely many integers $p$ satisfy the interval bound. Consequently, along EVERY sequence of pairwise distinct elements of $\mathcal S(K)$, $q\to\infty$ and the displayed inequality forces $p/q\to r_0$. The infinite set therefore has exactly one accumulation point in $\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$, namely the finite $r_0$. This proves both quantifiers needed when passing to arbitrary infinite subsets.

**All lifted paths are straight and parallel.** Apply step1.1 to any two points of any continuous lifted irreducible peripheral path and to a sequence of distinct elements of the FULL set. Divide by $q$ and use step3.1 to obtain $r_0(\alpha_1-\alpha_0)+(\beta_1-\beta_0)=0.$ Thus $\beta+r_0\alpha$ is constant on each path, and any nonconstant one lies on a line of slope $-r_0$. In particular the varying-meridian path of step2.1 contains every point of a nontrivial interval of that line: its $\alpha$ coordinate covers the whole endpoint interval by continuity. No finite-component or semialgebraic path-selection assertion is required for this implication.

**A nonzero Laurent equation actually vanishes on this arc.** For completeness the needed image-dimension operation is the accepted field-linear adjoint calculation [F2], not an assumption that the A-polynomial Definition excludes larger images. If a generic irreducible eigenline-incidence component had algebraically independent $M,L$, its function field would admit two derivations independently differentiating $M,L$; extend these through its finite separable algebraic part by the minimal-polynomial derivative formula. The actual boundary homology has dimension two. Self-duality and the pair exact sequence make both boundary inclusion and cohomological restriction rank one. The actual word/eigenbasis pairing therefore puts ALL logarithmic derivative pairs $(DL/L,DM/M)$ in the same line, contradicting those two independent derivations. Reducible components have $L=1$ by knot abelianization. All peripheral images thus have dimension at most one. The finitely many zero-dimensional image components give only finitely many points. The nonconstant interval of step4.1, after discarding these points, lies in the union of the one-dimensional image curves; hence the nonzero Laurent polynomial $A_K$ in [F3] vanishes on it. By continuity it vanishes on the entire interval. This argument allows arbitrary dimensions of the underlying character components and does not confuse a one-parameter family with a maximal image component.

**Rationality by a finite exponential calculation.** Write $A_K(M,L)=\sum_{(a,b)\in T}c_{ab}M^aL^b$, with finite distinct integral pairs and nonzero coefficients. On the interval $M=e^{i\alpha}$, $L=e^{i(c-r_0\alpha)}$, step5.1 gives $\sum_{(a,b)\in T} c_{ab}e^{ibc}e^{i(a-r_0b)\alpha}=0.$ If $r_0$ were irrational, all real numbers $a-r_0b$ would be distinct: equality for different pairs would either force identical pairs or express $r_0$ as a ratio of integers. Differentiate this finite identity $0,1,\ldots,|T|-1$ times at an interior point. Its coefficient matrix is a Vandermonde matrix in the distinct numbers $i(a-r_0b)$, multiplied by nonzero diagonal exponentials. Its determinant is nonzero, forcing every $c_{ab}e^{ibc}=0$, contrary to their choice. Thus $r_0\in\mathbb Q$. This proves rationality without importing a transcendence-number theorem or claiming arithmetic algebraicity of isolated pillowcase points.

**Full package with explicit external inputs.** Steps1.1–6.1 prove the elementary full-set boundedness, uniqueness and rationality operation from [L1]. The actual alternative is now supplied externally by [L1], while [L2] supplies the additional nonzero bound, L-space surgery, fiberedness, Alexander and satellite interfaces. The accepted filling and closed-lift operations [F4], together with the external knot-exterior trichotomy in [L2], give the geometric reductions required in §§3–5. These establish all four parts of the original package under its stated hypotheses. This completion uses external gauge and classification results; it does not assert local reconstructions of those results.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$ be the oriented primitive slope curve in the standard Heegaard torus, and let $\rho_t(z_1,z_2)=(e^{2\pi i p t}z_1,e^{2\pi i q t}z_2)$ be the weighted circle action on the unit $S^3\subset\mathbb C^2$. Choose $N(K)$ to be a sufficiently small closed metric tube around the orbit $K$ for the round metric; this tube is invariant because $\rho_t$ is isometric and preserves $K$. Set $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Let $x$ and $y$ be based generators of the fundamental groups of the two solid-torus pieces obtained by cutting $E_K$ along the annulus left on the Heegaard torus, oriented so that the annulus core maps to $x^p$ and $y^q$. Then

$$\pi_1(E_K)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle.$$

The common element $h=x^p=y^q$ is central and represents a regular fiber of a Seifert fibration of $E_K$ over a disk. The fibration has two distinguished core fibers of multiplicities $|p|$ and $|q|$; a fiber of multiplicity one is regular, and a fiber of multiplicity greater than one is exceptional. Thus there are exactly two exceptional fibers when $|p|,|q|>1$, and one is regular when one absolute parameter is $1$.

For any integers $\alpha,\beta$ with $p\alpha+q\beta=1$, compatible based paths identify the positive normal-disk meridian and preferred longitude in the peripheral system as

$$\mu=y^\alpha x^\beta,\qquad \lambda=h\mu^{-pq}.$$

Here the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and the preferred longitude has degree one around $K$ and maps to zero in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$. Their homology classes form a basis of $H_1(\partial E_K;\mathbb Z)$, so both classes are primitive.

Assume full AC. Let $P\subset V=S^1\times D^2$ be an oriented smooth pattern of signed winding $w$, let $C\subset S^3$ be an oriented smooth companion, and form $K=P(C)$ by the specified zero-framed oriented tubular embedding. Let $P(U)$ denote its closure under the zero-framed unknotted embedding of the same product solid torus. Write $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$, with outer product marking $(\mu_V,\lambda_V)$. On its inner torus use $(\mu_P,\lambda_P)$, where $\lambda_P$ is the preferred longitude of $P(U)$. Then
$$H_1(X_P;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu_P]\oplus\mathbb Z[\lambda_V],\qquad [\mu_V]=w[\mu_P],\qquad [\lambda_P]=w[\lambda_V].$$
The inner marking becomes exactly the preferred marking $(\mu_K,\lambda_K)$ after satellite gluing. Compatible access paths are retained; arbitrary changes conjugate the corresponding group restrictions and do not change these homology or eigenvalue assertions.

Every irreducible representation of $\pi_1(E_{P(U)})$ extends, after restriction to $X_P$, to an irreducible representation of $\pi_1(E_K)$ with the identical inner peripheral eigenvalues. For $w\ne0$, every one-dimensional irreducible-character peripheral image curve of $C$ has a finite function-field cover carrying an actual irreducible satellite representation whose eigenvalues satisfy
$$M_K^w=M_C,\qquad L_K=L_C^w.$$
Here the common peripheral eigenline is part of the data. No pointwise simultaneous diagonalization at parabolic exceptional points is asserted.

In particular, suppose the enhanced polynomial of $K$ has support on a line of primitive direction $(q,p)$, where the exponent pair $(a,b)$ denotes $L^aM^b$. Then the enhanced polynomial of $P(U)$ has support on a line of the same direction. If $w\ne0$, the enhanced polynomial of $C$ has support on a line of direction $(q w^2,p)$, reduced to a primitive vector when necessary. Unit enhanced polynomials, with one-point support, are included. Thus for a finite slope $r=p/q$, $q\ne0$, pattern closure is $r$-thin and companion is $(r/w^2)$-thin. No assertion that $w\ne0$, that $P(U)$ is nontrivial, or that any knot is fibered or an instanton L-space knot is made here.

Assume countable choice. Let $K:S^1	o S^3$ be a smooth oriented embedding and write its quotient normal bundle as $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$. Choose an orientation-preserving trivialization $
u_K\cong S^1	imes\mathbb R^2$ and a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega	o S^3$, meaning a smooth embedding from an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq
u_K$ of the zero section onto an open neighbourhood of $K(S^1)$ with $\Phi(s,0)=K(s)$, such that in these product coordinates $\Omega$ contains $S^1	imes D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$. Here $D^2_r=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:\|z\|\le r\}$ uses the product Euclidean norm induced by the chosen trivialization. Set $N(K)=\Phi(S^1	imes D^2_\epsilon)$, $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T_K=\partial E_K$, and let $i:T_K\hookrightarrow E_K$ be inclusion, $p:T_K	o S^1$ the product projection, and $\mu$ the positive boundary of a normal disk, using the normal-plane orientation determined by the orientations of $K$ and $S^3$. A class is primitive if it is not $m$ times another class for any integer $|m|>1$. Then $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is generated by $[\mu]$. The kernel of $i_*:H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)	o H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is a primitive rank-one direct summand generated by a unique class $[\lambda]$ with $p_*[\lambda]=1\in H_1(S^1;\mathbb Z)$. It has a simple closed representative, is the preferred longitude, and $([\mu],[\lambda])$ is a basis of $H_1(T_K;\mathbb Z)$.

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $p,q\in\mathbb Z$ be coprime and not both zero, and let $E_K(p/q)$ be the Dehn filling whose attached solid-torus meridian is identified with $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$. A closed 3-manifold $Y$ is **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian** if every homomorphism $\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ has abelian image. The slope $p/q$ is an **$SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian surgery slope** for $K$ if $E_K(p/q)$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The knot admits infinitely many such surgeries if infinitely many distinct rational slopes have this property.

Assume full AC. Let $K=P(C)$ be a zero-framed oriented satellite, with signed pattern winding $w$, and let $P(U)$ be its zero-framed pattern closure. If a slope $p/q$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian for $K$, it is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian for $P(U)$.

If $w\ne0$, $\gcd(p,q)=1$ and $q>0$, put $d=\gcd(q,w^2)$. If the primitive satellite filling of slope
$$\frac{p w^2/d}{q/d}=w^2\frac pq$$
is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian, then the companion filling of slope $p/q$ is $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian. The meridional case $q=0$ also holds, since both meridional filling groups are trivial. This is an assertion about ALL representations, including reducible nonabelian ones, not merely irreducible characters. Consequently infinitely many distinct rational $SL_2(\mathbb C)$-abelian satellite slopes give infinitely many such slopes for the pattern closure and, when $w\ne0$, for the companion after division by $w^2$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be the interior of a compact connected orientable three-manifold with $k\ge1$ torus cusps and a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. Choose an ordered peripheral basis on each cusp. For cusp $i$, let the generalized filling parameter sphere be $S_i=\mathbb R^2\cup\{\infty\}$, with $\infty$ denoting the complete cusp and primitive integral pairs modulo sign denoting ordinary slopes. There is a neighborhood $U$ of $(\infty,\ldots,\infty)$ in $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ such that every tuple in $U$ whose finite coordinates are primitive integral slopes determines a complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric on the corresponding ordinary Dehn filling; coordinates equal to $\infty$ remain unfilled complete cusps. Consequently, one may choose neighborhoods $U_i$ of $\infty$ with $\prod_i U_i\subseteq U$, and only finitely many primitive integral pairs at each cusp lie outside $U_i$. Thus every simultaneous filling whose slopes all lie in their respective $U_i$ is hyperbolic. Nonprimitive ray parameters may describe cone or orbifold completions but are not ordinary smooth fillings. No universal numeric length threshold or universal bound on the number of exceptional slopes is asserted.

Assume AC. Every nonempty connected oriented complete Riemannian three-manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$ is isometric to $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^3$ for a discrete torsion-free subgroup $\Gamma\le\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$. The covering is a universal Riemannian covering and identifies $\Gamma$ with the fundamental group up to the usual basepoint conjugacies. Its completeness and quotient presentation are conclusions from the stated metric hypotheses. The orientation-preserving isometry group of the model is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ with its usual Möbius boundary action.

Assume full AC. Let $Y$ be a nonempty closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold equipped with a complete Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Its faithful discrete holonomy
$$\rho:\pi_1(Y)\longrightarrow PSL_2(\mathbb C)$$
admits a homomorphism lift $\widetilde\rho:\pi_1(Y)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ through the quotient by $\{I,-I\}$. The lift is faithful. The required Spin structure on $TY$ is actually constructed from a finite complete Heegaard splitting, rather than assumed from the vanishing of a knot exterior's second cohomology.
If $p:E\to B$ is a finite-sheeted covering, then $E$ is compact if and only if $B$ is compact.

Assume full AC. Let a smooth fibered satellite knot be written $K=P(C)$ with essential companion torus $T$, nontrivial companion $C$, and pattern not isotopic to the core of its solid torus. Let $w$ be its signed winding number. Then $w\ne0$ and
$$g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C).$$
More precisely, a product decomposition obtained by cutting the given fiber produces connected-surface mapping-torus descriptions of the companion and pattern-closure exteriors, with fiber surfaces of their minimal Seifert genera. If the symmetric Alexander polynomial of $K$ has nonzero coefficients in both its highest degree and the immediately next degree, then $P(U)$ is nontrivial. No instanton theorem is assumed or proved by this assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, its Seifert genus is zero if and only if $K$ is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary orientation equal to that of $K$, let $g$ satisfy $\chi(F)=1-2g$, and choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Use the positive normal convention $(n,u,v)>0$ and define $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K=H_1(\widetilde X_K;\mathbb Z)$ be the one-variable Alexander module of the knot complement $X_K=S^3\setminus K$, where the cover is classified by the total-linking homomorphism and $t$ acts by the deck transformation corresponding to the positive meridian. Then there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$-modules
$$A_K\cong\operatorname{coker}\bigl(V-tV^T:\Lambda^{2g}\to\Lambda^{2g}\bigr).$$

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$, with $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ and use the positive normal convention $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $A_K$ be the first homology of the infinite cyclic cover of $S^3\setminus K$ classified by total linking, with $t$ acting by the positive-meridian deck transformation. Let $\Delta_K(t)$ be the generator of the zeroth elementary ideal $E_0(A_K)$ in $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, and write $p\doteq q$ when $p$ and $q$ differ by a unit $\pm t^k$ of $\Lambda$. Then for every such $F$ and basis,

$$\det(V-tV^T)\doteq\Delta_K(t).$$

The determinant is $1$ for the empty $0\times0$ matrix when $g=0$. This formula concerns the polynomial $\Delta_K$; the existing knot-normalized fraction $D_K=\Delta_K/(1-t)$ is a separate invariant.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $K=T(p,q)$, and put $a=|p|$, $b=|q|$. For $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, define
$$\delta_{a,b}(t)=\frac{(t^{ab}-1)(t-1)}{(t^a-1)(t^b-1)}.$$
Then $\delta_{a,b}(t)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[t]$, the Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K$ defined as a generator of the zeroth elementary ideal of the positive-meridian infinite-cyclic-cover module satisfies $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\delta_{a,b}(t)$, and the knot genus is $g(K)=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. Here $f\doteq g$ means $f=\pm t^k g$ for some integer $k$.

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a knot. The input package required by the Baldwin–Sivek thin-knot and infinitely-many-abelian-surgeries arguments consists of the following conclusions with their stated hypotheses: (i) a nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-averse knot has a unique rational accumulation slope and either it or its mirror is an instanton L-space knot; (ii) a nontrivial instanton L-space knot is fibered and its symmetrized Alexander polynomial has coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ with nonzero coefficients alternating in sign; (iii) the L-space satellite restrictions and the pattern/companion surgery-transfer statements exclude the satellite cases used in §§3–5; and (iv) the hyperbolic Dehn-filling theorem and the knot-exterior JSJ classification reduce the remaining cases to torus knots. This carrier records the exact imported result interfaces and does not assert that these conclusions have been proved locally.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $E_K$ be the compact connected orientable exterior of a smooth knot in $S^3$, with one torus boundary component. If $E_K$ is irreducible, its boundary is incompressible, $E_K$ is atoroidal, and $E_K$ is not Seifert-fibered, then $\operatorname{int}(E_K)$ admits a complete finite-volume Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $-1$ with one torus cusp. No conclusion is asserted for a torus or satellite knot unless its exterior satisfies all four topological hypotheses.

derivations.claim: **The full torus direction by its actual group.** Let $K=T(a,b)$ with signed coprime nonzero parameters. For every positive integer $n$, the rational slope $(abn+1)/n$ is primitive since $\gcd(abn+1,n)=1$. Its filling relation is $\mu^{abn+1}\lambda^n=\mu h^n=1$ by [F1]. Since $h$ is central, the meridian becomes central. It normally generates, so the entire quotient group is cyclic and EVERY representation has abelian image. The slopes $ab+1/n$ are distinct. This proves the direction for all signed torus knots, including the unit-parameter unknot, without an unproved lens-surgery classification or a restriction to irreducible representations.

**Actual closed lifts exclude the supplied hyperbolic case.** For a primitive rational slope $p/q$ with $p\ne0$, filling abelianization is $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$: quotient the meridian-generated exterior abelianization by $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]=p[\mu]$. At each all-but-finitely-many hyperbolic filling in [F3], its closed metric has a faithful SL2 lift. An abelian image would make the whole group abelian and hence that finite cyclic group. Its universal cover $\mathbb H^3$ would then be a finite-sheet cover of a closed compact space and so compact, a contradiction. Thus every such nonzero hyperbolic filling has a nonabelian representation. Discarding the single zero slope is harmless. This proves that a supplied finite-volume hyperbolic knot has only finitely many SL2-abelian rational fillings; the closed Spin lift, not the exterior's second cohomology, is essential.

**Filling transfer and the exact conditional limit argument.** Every SL2-abelian filling is SU2-abelian since $SU(2)\subset SL_2(\mathbb C)$. For a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian essential satellite WITH the actual fibered and adjacent-top properties, apply [F4], giving $w\ne0$ and nontrivial pattern closure. In the final reduction these properties are supplied by choosing the actual knot or mirror furnished by [L1] before this row is invoked. Fact [F2] supplies infinitely many actual SL2-abelian slopes for $P(U)$ and $C$, namely $r_i$ and $r_i/w^2$ from distinct satellite slopes $r_i$. Under [L1], the original SU2-abelian slope set is bounded; every infinite subset therefore has a convergent subsequence, and uniqueness of its accumulation point makes its limit $r(K)$. Indeed infinitely many distinct points outside any fixed neighborhood of that point would have a second accumulation point by compactness of a bounded closed interval. Thus the transferred subsets have limits $r(K)$ and $r(K)/w^2$. Applying [L1] to the nontrivial components identifies $r(P(U))=r(K)=w^2r(C)$. No assertion that a mere infinite subset shares a finite accumulation point without boundedness has been used.

**Conditional minimal-genus reduction.** By [L2] and step1.2, a nontrivial infinitely-SL2-abelian nontorus knot would be an essential satellite. Choose such a satellite of least genus. By [L1], one of this knot and its mirror has the actual fibered and specified Alexander properties. Reflection reverses the positive meridian and preserves the degree-one zero-homology longitude by [F1]; the resulting exterior group isomorphism therefore identifies its filling groups with those at negated slopes. It also carries spanning surfaces in both directions, preserving minimal genus, and sends torus knots to torus knots. Replace the least-genus counterexample by that chosen mirror if needed, and choose its essential satellite decomposition by [L2] and step1.2. We now use its ACTUAL supplied fiber and Alexander properties, without an extra assumption on mirror invariance of those coefficients. Thus [F4] and step1.3 give nontrivial $P(U),C$, nonzero $w$, and $g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C)$. Both positive genera are strictly smaller, even for $|w|=1$. Each component has infinitely many SL2-abelian slopes by [F2], so minimality and [L2], with step1.2, make both torus knots. For a signed torus knot the cyclic filling family in step1.1 accumulates at the parameter product; the uniqueness in [L1] identifies its limit slope with that product. Their signed parameter products have the same nonzero sign by step1.3. Let $a>b\ge2$ and $c>d\ge2$ be their respective ABSOLUTE parameter pairs, interchanging parameters when needed. Taking absolute values of that slope relation gives $ab=cdw^2$. The symmetric torus polynomial in [F5] depends only on these absolute parameters, so no further mirroring of the actual satellite and no extra instanton property for either component is needed.

We supply the classical satellite Alexander formula used in [L2], instead of assuming it from a satellite Definition. Write $X=V\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu P$ for the pattern exterior and $E_K=X\cup_T E_C$ for the satellite exterior, with outer meridian $\mu_V$ identified with $\mu_C$ and preferred outer longitude with $\lambda_C$. Let $w\ne0$ be the winding number, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ act on covers by the satellite's positive-meridian deck transformation. Total linking restricts to $w$ times companion linking on $E_C$, to $w$ on $\mu_V$ and zero on the outer longitude. The pulled-back cover of $T$ has $|w|$ cylinder components, so $H_1(\widetilde T)=\Lambda/(t^w-1)$ generated by a lift of $\lambda_C$; its $H_0$ is the same module. The cover of $E_C$ has $|w|$ components, with module $H_1=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C$, where $s$ acts by $t^w$. Its $H_0$ map from $T$ is an isomorphism, because the two linking images are the same subgroup $w\mathbb Z$. Its longitude class is zero in $H_1$: a Seifert surface for $C$ lifts, since linking vanishes on all its loops by normal push-off, and its boundary is that lifted longitude. Replace $C$ by the unknot to obtain the pattern closure $P(U)$. Its companion-side cover has $|w|$ contractible components, the same $H_0$ and zero $H_1$. In both lifted Mayer–Vietoris sequences the $H_0$ map is injective, since its companion-side coordinate is an isomorphism. The only $H_1(\widetilde T)$ image is consequently in the SAME pattern-side module. Quotienting that image yields, respectively, $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}\oplus\bigl(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C\bigr)$. All gluings and the chosen longitude bounds are in the actual peripheral marking; no companion character transfer is used in this module calculation.

For $w\ne0$, $\Lambda$ is free of rank $|w|$ over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$ via $s=t^w$, with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{|w|-1}$ after reversing the exponent convention if $w<0$. Extension of scalars is therefore exact, and [F5] supplies a square presentation of its companion summand by the companion Seifert matrix with $s$ replaced by $t^w$. The direct sum in step 3.1 has a block-diagonal square presentation. Taking its determinant gives $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\Delta_{P(U)}(t)\Delta_C(t^w)$. With symmetric normalization and value one at $t=1$, the Laurent unit ambiguity disappears. The winding-zero case gives the same polynomial identity with $\Delta_C(1)=1$: its companion-side cover is now a disjoint union of copies of $E_C$, with $H_1=\Lambda[\mu_C]$ and $H_0=\Lambda$. The torus-side groups are $H_1=\Lambda^2$, $H_0=\Lambda$, and the meridian map onto the companion $H_1$ is an isomorphism while the longitude maps to zero. The same maps hold for an unknot companion. Eliminate the companion meridian generator in both sequences; their identical remaining pattern quotient is $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}$. This proves the Alexander satellite formula also for $w=0$, without claiming that such a pattern can be an instanton L-space satellite.

Put $v=|w|$; the symmetric companion polynomial satisfies $\Delta_C(t^w)=\Delta_C(t^v)$. The finite torus-pattern obstruction is also elementary once the stated coefficient restrictions in [L1] have been supplied. Write $a>b\ge2$ coprime and $g=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. The formula in [F5], expanded at infinity, is $\Delta_{T_{a,b}}(t)=t^g(1-t^{-ab})(1-t^{-1})/((1-t^{-a})(1-t^{-b}))$. Modulo terms of degree at most $g-a$, its expansion is $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor a/b\rfloor}(t^{g-ib}-t^{g-ib-1})$. Thus, for $0\le v<a$, its coefficient $c_{g-v}$ is $1$ if $v=0\pmod b$, $-1$ if $v=1\pmod b$, and zero otherwise. Suppose the companion's normalized polynomial has leading terms $t^h-t^{h-1}+O(t^{h-2})$ and the satellite's nonzero coefficients alternate with absolute value one, exactly the two externally supplied instanton conclusions in [L1]. By step 4.1 its coefficient in degree $g+hv-v$ is $c_{g-v}-1$. If $v=1\pmod b$ this is $-2$, impossible. If $v=qb+r$ with $2\le r<b$, it is $-1$, while the preceding nonzero coefficient is the $-1$ in degree $g+hv-qb-1$: all intervening torus coefficients vanish and no lower companion term reaches those degrees. These consecutive negative coefficients contradict alternation. Consequently $b$ divides $v$ whenever $0<v<a$. This argument is a proved finite polynomial implication and uses the externally supplied instanton properties, without proving their gauge-theoretic foundations.

In particular the torus-pattern configuration required by the minimal-satellite argument is incompatible with those coefficient restrictions. If $ab=k v^2$ for an integer $k\ge1$, then $v<a$, since otherwise $ab\ge a^2>ab$. Step 5.1 makes $b\mid v$, whence $a=k b(v/b)^2$ contradicts $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $b\ge2$. Mirroring a torus pattern does not change its symmetric Alexander polynomial, so the same contradiction applies after the prescribed mirror reduction. Also $v=1$ is already excluded as soon as both nontrivial pattern and companion have leading terms $t^g-t^{g-1}$ and $t^h-t^{h-1}$: their product has second leading coefficient $-2$. This is the finite polynomial contradiction needed for the conditional configuration in step2.1; it does not supply the externally supplied instanton conclusions.

The companion torus in step2.1 has the adjacent leading terms required in step5.1 by its explicit torus formula [F5], without another instanton hypothesis on that companion. With $v=|w|$, the configuration of step2.1 satisfies $ab=cdv^2$; applying step6.1 to this positive $v$ gives a contradiction. Steps1.1–1.2 unconditionally prove the full signed-torus direction and the supplied-metric hyperbolic exclusion; [F2] proves all actual pattern/companion filling cases. Steps1.3–6.1 supply the remaining converse assembly with the exact externally supplied or explicitly conditional premises [L1, L2]. The exact full iff is now supplied independently by [F6], rather than claimed as a newly local gauge or hyperbolization proof. The original full Statement and representation scope remain unchanged.

Apply [F6] to the given smooth knot. Its rational filling and all-representations abelian conventions coincide with the Statement, and its torus convention includes the unknot. It gives the converse to the locally proved signed-torus direction and hence the full original equivalence.

The converse proceeds by excluding hyperbolic knots via all-but-finitely-many hyperbolic fillings with faithful nonabelian holonomy representations, then excluding satellites via the Baldwin–Sivek pattern/companion surgery transfer and instanton L-space restrictions. The missing supplier hypotheses are recorded in [A1]; neither the cited theorem nor the unresolved module is accepted as a local proof. This theorem is escalated.
